root_motivation: Grounding: opportunity -- visions/mcphost-aistack-harvest.md addendum 2026-09-30 (drift pattern), ported from ~/projects/ai-stack @ 4ef6c22 aistack-observability (store.rs grounding_records/definition_versions/drift_queue/emitted_reviews, drift.rs DriftDetector/on_version_change/QuestionDelta, review.rs DriftReviewItem, alert.rs AlertEvent, eval.rs's EvalHarness stub replaced with deterministic re-execution). After PRD-mcphost-table-context-and-sql-passthrough, the query log holds every SQL statement with its row count, documents carry a version, and table notes are annotations with updated_at and no version history -- but nothing links a change to the queries that depended on the changed thing, and nothing re-runs them. A note edit that fixes one question silently breaks another, and the only signal was the next complaint.
user_persona: A tenant who edits a table note, appends rows that change a column's inferred role, or uploads a new document version, and the agent that answered questions from the previous state and needs to know which earlier answers are now stale.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a table note change through host.table.model_set, When the tick runs, Then context_versions has a new row for that target and a drift_queue entry with status queued, then done within 60 s.
Given 12 logged queries naming expenses and a note change on it, When the review is produced, Then it holds 12 deltas, changed_count 0, regressed_count 0, and no alert is written.
Given the same change applied twice with identical content, When both are processed, Then one review item exists.
Given an append that changes a column's inferred role, When the review runs, Then a logged GROUP BY over that column shows before.row_count 7 and after.row_count 31 with changed: true.

Given a logged query that now errors after a schema change, When reviewed, Then its delta carries after.error_code, regressed_count is at least 1, and a drift_regression alert with severity warning exists.
Given a document uploaded as version 3 and 5 logged searches whose top hits included version 2, When reviewed, Then 5 search deltas exist and any with top-5 overlap under 3 counts as regressed.
Given host.drift.resolve(item_id, "cosmetic"), When host.drift.reviews(open_only: true) is called, Then the item is absent and host.drift.review(item_id) shows the reason.
Given two tenants, When tenant A reads reviews, Then none of tenant B's appear.
Given 50 affected queries on the fixture, When a change is processed, Then re-runs finish under 5 s on the builder and the tenant's daily call count rose by one.
Given host.drift.check("expenses") with no version change, When the tick runs, Then a review with the current deltas is produced.

Given prod after land, When a fresh tenant loads the fixture, runs three queries over expenses, changes the table note, and calls host.drift.reviews, Then one open review lists three deltas with changed_count 0 (Live; evidence: mcphost-1 healthz version after deploy plus the reviews response in the receipt under docs/receipts/).
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred (Live) -- operator-provisioned: needs a real run against production after deploy, with the receipt committed under docs/receipts/; this coder dispatch never provisions, resizes, deletes, or reconfigures any server, volume, or service, so AC11 is declared deferred rather than faked.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a python tool, When it calls mcphost.drift.reviews(), Then it receives the same list the tool returns.

scope: src/drift/ (new): versions.rs (context_versions write hooks), queue.rs (drift_queue enqueue + content dedupe hash), rerun.rs (the tick-driven re-run engine: SQL AST table-name extraction, dependent-query/search lookup, QueryDelta/SearchDelta, regression detection), review.rs (host.drift.reviews/review/resolve), alert.rs (drift_alerts on regression).
src/db.rs: migration 0066 (context_versions, drift_queue, emitted_reviews, drift_reviews, drift_alerts) and the Db methods/row structs over them.
src/tables.rs: a new _docs_search_log-sibling sample_hash column on _mcphost_query_log, log_query extended to write it, run_query_sync made pub(crate) for rerun.rs's reuse.

src/tables_model.rs: model_set and tick_once each call the new versions:: hooks (table_note / table_schema changes); tick_once also drains the drift queue via drift::rerun::tick_once at the end of its own 10s cycle.

src/docs.rs: doc_put calls versions::record_document_change on a real content change; doc_search split into a logging wrapper plus a non-logging search_core, with a new rerun_search helper for drift's own internal re-runs so they never re-log themselves into _docs_search_log.
src/handler.rs: four new tenant tools (host.drift.reviews/review/resolve/check) and (AC12) a TenantDriftBridge bridging CallCtx.drift to drift::reviews for the python sandbox.
src/kinds/mod.rs, src/kinds/python.rs, src/runs.rs: DriftBackend/NoDrift plumbing and the mcphost.drift python shim (AC12).
Cargo.toml: minor version bump 0.78.0 -> 0.79.0 per this PRD's build_version_bump field.

Gate artifacts kept in sync with the new tool surface: contracts/host-tools.v1.json, www/llms.txt, docs/kinds/python.md, plugin/skills/mcphost/SKILL.md, plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, scripts/gen-test-suites.sh (sandbox suite cap).
non_goals: Judging whether a changed answer is better or worse -- the review shows the diff; a person or the loop decides (PRD non-goal).
Model-based evaluation of any kind -- eval.rs's EvalHarness is replaced with deterministic re-execution, not ported (PRD non-goal / technical considerations).
Drift on host.state key-value data (PRD non-goal).
Retention beyond 90 days of review items -- left to the existing purge tick, not newly implemented here (PRD non-goal).

Requirement 9 (host.drift.stats) and requirement 11 (P2 value diff for queries under 100 rows) are P1/P2 requirements in the PRD body with no corresponding acceptance criterion in the PRD's own AC list (1-12) and were not in this dispatch's assigned AC list -- left unimplemented, not deferred, since they were never in scope for this pass.

five_whys_trace.q: Why re-run the stored SQL/search deterministically instead of porting ai-stack's eval.rs (an external evaluator)?
five_whys_trace.a: mcphost already has the real, read-only execution path (host.table.query's guards, host.docs.search's ranking) that produced the original logged result -- re-running the same path and diffing is strictly more deterministic and cheaper than calling out to an evaluator, and the PRD's own technical considerations say exactly this ('mcphost can do better by re-running the stored SQL, or the stored search, and diffing').

five_whys_trace.q: Why two separate dedupe mechanisms (a unique index on drift_queue's (tenant_id, kind, target, trigger_version) vs emitted_reviews' content hash) rather than one?
five_whys_trace.a: AC1 requires every distinct context_versions row to be queued (so a tenant can see each edit was processed), but AC3 requires that applying the identical note value twice -- two distinct versions, identical content -- still produces only one review. Queue-level dedup (per exact version) and review-level dedup (per content hash) are different questions; collapsing them into one would fail one of the two ACs.

five_whys_trace.q: Why version every table-model tick recompute as a 'table_schema change' unconditionally, rather than diffing old vs new column roles to decide if anything really changed?
five_whys_trace.a: AC4's own scenario (an append that changes row counts under a GROUP BY) is really a question about data, not about the model's own role/type inference changing at all -- the tick recompute is conceptually the re-assessment event the PRD means by 'table schema' drift, and versioning every recompute lets the natural re-run (seeing a different row count) carry the signal, with no separate role-diff logic needed.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does AC5 use host.table.drop rather than an ALTER-COLUMN-style operation to produce a genuinely erroring re-run?
five_whys_trace.a: The host.table.* API has no column-type-narrowing or ALTER-COLUMN operation that could make a previously-valid SELECT start erroring; dropping the table after a change is already queued (but before the tick drains it) is the one real operation in the existing surface that turns a previously-successful logged query into a genuine 'no such table' SQLite error at re-run time, which is what AC5's Then actually requires.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does host.drift.reviews/review/resolve/check get its own 'since' version in contracts/host-tools.v1.json, or does it inherit the CONTRACT_BASELINE_SINCE every pre-existing tool shares?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Added a dedicated HOST_DRIFT_SINCE = "0.79.0" constant in src/api_contract.rs (matching this PRD's own version-bump commit), following the same precedent host.changelog's own HOST_CHANGELOG_SINCE already set, rather than letting four brand-new tools silently report the 0.58.0 baseline.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should drift's own internal re-run of a logged search write a new row to _docs_search_log?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- doing so would make drift::rerun's own background re-run look like a new dependent search, which a later tick would then pick up again, compounding forever. docs::doc_search was split into a logging/metering wrapper plus a non-logging search_core, with a new docs::rerun_search helper (search_core only) used exclusively by drift::rerun::rerun_document.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should drift_alerts reuse the existing host-wide alerts table/raise() infra in src/alerts.rs?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- a dedicated drift_alerts table (migration 0066) was added instead, so this PRD controls the exact severity strings ("warning"/"critical") and shape the PRD's own AlertEvent {kind, severity, detail} names, independent of the existing AlertConfig/Severity enum's own semantics.
